content.text:
The build succeeds. The warning comes from Apple’s linker: the debug executable’s `__eh_frame` section is **27.45 MiB**, exceeding the linker’s stated **16 MiB** limit for encoding DWARF unwind offsets in its compact unwind table. It concerns metadata used to unwind the stack, including during Rust panics.

There’s also a reason you may only be seeing it now: **Rust 1.97 started displaying linker output from successful builds**, which earlier versions hid. You’re using Rust 1.98.1. An [open upstream issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/159105) reports the same warning after upgrading to 1.97. [Rust 1.97 release notes](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2026/07/09/Rust-1.97.0/)

The default development profile uses no optimization and unwinding for panics. [Cargo profile documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html) The recent [Polars addition in PR #41](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/41) may have increased the amount of unwind metadata, but we haven’t established that it first pushed the executable over the limit.

Confidence is high in the immediate cause and the change in warning visibility. We don’t know when this project first exceeded the limit or whether the warning has any measurable runtime impact.

- Source control: dependency manifests, Git history/blame, PRs #41, #25, and #23.
